editorial_policy: Safe-for-work, source-linked factoids. 'Documented' means a source establishes the described historical record, not that every related allegation is proven. 'Preliminary research' identifies findings that have not completed peer review. No extraordinary claims are presented as established.

factoids.title: A UFO study that measured the ordinary
factoids.fact: A three-site infrared camera experiment near Las Vegas reconstructed 365 well-tracked aerial objects from one week in May 2026. Researchers matched 284 to aircraft, found 17 more with aircraft-like motion but no aircraft ID, and identified 64 as small clouds. None showed anomalous motion in this sample.
factoids.caveat: The October 2026 manuscript is a preprint, not yet peer-reviewed. Its detection limits and one-week sample do not settle the wider UAP question; the 17 unidentified tracks are not evidence of extraordinary technology.

sources.title: Loeb et al., An Assessment of the Triangulation Capabilities of a Multi-Site All-Sky Infrared Camera Array

factoids.title: The Cold War wiretap room with 40 tape recorders
factoids.fact: Declassified CIA records describe LIENVOY, a joint U.S.–Mexican telephone-surveillance operation that targeted diplomatic lines and Mexican political figures. The CIA station history lists 40 Ampex voice recorders among the equipment installed for the listening post.
factoids.caveat: This establishes a historical surveillance program, not any theory about who assassinated President Kennedy. Major portions of the CIA's Mexico City station history remain redacted.

sources.title: CIA Mexico City Station History [Extracts], JFK Records document 104-10414-10124
National Security Archive, The CIA Station in Mexico: The Last JFK Assassination Records Secrets
